_comment: Example manifest for: python tools/meshy_import.py --batch <this file> --yes-spend-credits
List it first, without spending: python tools/meshy_import.py --batch <this file> --dry-run
Each entry is ONE paid generation (text: preview + refine = 30 credits with ai_model latest;
image: 30). Output: resources/reference/meshy/<era>/ . An entry whose
<stem>.provenance.json already exists is skipped, so a stopped batch can be re-run.
The batch stops when the next generation would leave fewer than --budget-floor credits (591).
Per entry: era, name, kind (building|prop|item), size (metres along size_axis: x|y|z|longest),
and exactly one of prompt (<= 800 characters) or image (URL, or a path relative to this file
or to the repository root). Optional: tier, also_tier, map, default_material, clusters,
preview, reduce, note, and the generation parameters ai_model, should_remesh,
target_polycount, topology, geometry_resolution, texture, texture_resolution, enable_pbr,
texture_prompt, remove_lighting. 'defaults' is merged under every entry.
THE SIZES BELOW ARE PLACEHOLDERS that show the format; they are not sourced dimensions.
A size typed into a real manifest needs its own citation (grounding-auditor).

entries.name: example_strip_building_from_image
entries.note: image-to-3D from a sourced reference image; this path is an example and does not exist

entries.name: example_strip_building_from_text
entries.prompt: Single-storey Roman strip building, gable end to the street, timber portico, red clay tile roof, plain flat ground, no people, no vegetation

entries.name: example_amphora
entries.prompt: Roman transport amphora, plain fired clay, standing upright
